  "partial_result": "**Decision: fund one lever, negative-margin SmoothAP on the control family (A/C readout, frozen encoder), gated by a CPU-only FIT margin census before any paid training.** No edits, jobs, or native work were done. One caveat: I could not read docs/inshop_smooth_ap_plan_2026-10-04.md within budget, so check it for a prior SmoothAP-margin decision before freezing.\n\n## What the census actually supports\n\n| Fact (all four endpoints, 44 shared errors) | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Best-positive median rank, control / candidate | 3 / 2.5, max 33, 37 of 44 within rank 10 |\n| Positive minus impostor margin, median control / candidate | about -0.08 / -0.057, all 176 strictly negative |\n| Same impostor product across all four endpoints | 41 of 44 |\n| Error products with exactly two gallery positives | 29 of 44 |\n| Best positive is a different view than the query | 42 of 44 |\n| Impostor shares the query's view | 21 control / 19 candidate |\n| Errors involving the 81-image product id_00003523 (as query or impostor) | 7 of 44 |\n| Mutual confusion pairs among the 44 | 2 pairs (697/2663, 4854/7790) plus the 3523 hub |\n\nSupported: the core is a stable near-miss boundary owned by the frozen substrate plus this readout family and FIT data, not seed noise. The connected candidate shrank the median gap by roughly a quarter but flipped none. Not supported: missing information versus objective failure, label noise, view-nuisance causation (no base rate exists for the 1690 correct queries), and whether FIT geometry is thin. The last one is measurable and is the falsifier.\n\n## Mechanism and why it is causally distinct\n\nThe accepted objective (scripts/train_siglip2_identity_diversity.py, loss_terms at line 1268, smooth_ap_terms at line 1225) is SmoothAP with temperature 0.01 plus prototype regression. A sigmoid at that temperature carries under one percent of its gradient once a pair is separated by 0.05 in cosine. The accepted first-B64 ranking loss is already 0.033 to 0.040 at step 128, so FIT ranking is near-saturated and the only pairs still receiving ranking gradient are near ties. The held errors sit at median gaps of 0.06 to 0.08, exactly the band the loss treats as inert. Hypothesis: the readout learns a boundary that is barely positive on FIT, and that thin boundary flips for unseen products with two gallery views. Demanding that FIT positives beat impostors by a margin m reactivates currently inert FIT pairs and widens the boundary the linear readout exports.\n\nThe change is one statement in loss_terms after the scores line, with m applied to negative columns only, so positive-positive comparisons and the rp/rt structure are untouched:\n\n```python\nscores = scores + margin * negative_mask   # negative_mask: eligible rows not in the anchor's positive set\n```\n\nPre-register m = 0.05, five temperatures, the point where the existing sigmoid gradient drops below one percent. It is derived from the loss, not from held statistics. Compute cost is one 16 by 6355 add per micro-batch, so the paired cost ratio should be about 1.00 against the unchanged 1.50 gate.\n\nThis differs from every closed arm: not capacity (connected MLP), not coverage (identity diversity), not gradient conflict (falsified), not gallery freshness (killed), not augmentation or mixing. The older compact-ranking recipe had a hinge margin of 0.05 (scripts/train_siglip2_compact_ranking.py line 92), but the accepted SmoothAP objective never carried one.\n\nAlternatives compared and rejected: raising the temperature also reweights already-wide pairs and degrades the AP approximation, so attribution is muddier; a best-positive-only R@1 surrogate is inert on saturated FIT without a margin, and adding both changes two things; more updates mostly reduce regression and the cost gate caps them; live positive forwards or bank refresh repeat the closed freshness plan; the data-coverage scope passes Fable's own K_near rule (10 of 44 are rank-2 non-mutual) but costs about five DGX-hours and the fixed-budget coverage test already showed no R@1 effect; view-conditioned negatives cover at most half the core and need the same un-saturation anyway.\n\n## Falsifier, qualification, and evaluation sequence\n\n1. **CPU FIT margin census, TRAIN-only, no training.** New script under 120 s and 1 GiB. Inputs: the accepted control061 and control069 terminal checkpoints and the CPU-v5 initializer. Load state views.canonical (6355 by 1152), target, ranking_bank, head, means, mu_train, A, C. Apply fullfeature_raw_features (line 882), normalize, form the 6355-square cosine matrix, exclude self via ranking_membership (line 1209), and record per FIT row the best-positive minus top-impostor margin. Also run the existing cpu_gradients closure (line 1507) on the first B64 with m = 0 and m = 0.05 to report ranking versus regression A/C norms and cosine. No images, no held rows, no held labels.\n2. **Rejection rule, fixed before the run.** Let q equal the held-core rate, 44 of 1734. If the FIT margin at quantile q is at or above 0.05 in both seeds, FIT already satisfies the demanded margin at the matched error rate and the lever has nothing to act on: REJECT without training. Pivot: close FIT-objective shaping for the frozen-encoder readout; the next axis is representation (coverage scope or deeper unfreeze) as a separate decision. Otherwise GO.\n3. **Source freeze.** In scripts/train_siglip2_connected_mlp.py, route the update seam at line 1004 to a private margin loss_terms built with the existing AST Substitute and inverse pattern from _initializer_runtime (line 314), so the pinned trainer file stays byte-identical. Pin m in RECIPE. Run the existing source tests.\n4. **Native small qualification.** CPU600 with the control061 initializer and discarded update, then mechanics1200 for both arms at seed 179061 with the uninterrupted-17 versus 8-plus-9 replay.\n5. **Fresh paired evaluation.** TRAIN3000 seed 179061, control with m = 0 and candidate with m = 0.05, both A/C only with frozen encoder; two exports at 1500; score700 on the same TRAIN-selection panel with unchanged scorer, packed semantics, bootstrap, floors, and cost gates. First-seed survival (positive sign, gain at least 0.002) admits seed 179069; full GO needs both seeds plus a positive product 95 percent lower bound. No sealed VAL or official read before that.\n\nConfound to disclose: the margin also raises the ranking loss and its gradient norm, so under the binding clip of 1.0 it shifts the ranking share of each update. The paired arm therefore tests margin SmoothAP as a package. Step 1's gradient readout gives the expected magnitude shift before training; a weight-only control is the follow-up attribution arm only if the candidate passes. Still unproved after a pass: transfer to official protocol, the view-nuisance story, and any effect on the 3523 hub, which is a gallery-density effect no FIT objective can target.",
